basic_info.title: A Knowledge Architecture Layer for Map Data in Autonomous Vehicles
basic_info.venue: 2020 23rd IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC), Rhodes, Greece, September 2020 (IEEE). Affiliations: BMW Car IT GmbH / Institute of Artificial Intelligence, University of Ulm.

method.input_representation: HD_map / map_data_formats / road_environment_model (per-format low-level ontologies abstracted into a generic high-level road-environment ontology)
method.notes: Two-tier knowledge architecture: format-specific low-level ontologies (e.g., NDS, HERE) feed a generic high-level road-environment ontology via rules. Adequacy validated on two use cases - lane-change notification and logical-inconsistency detection over real map data.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Realizes the P1b semantic-enrichment idea SYMBOLICALLY via OWL/RDF ontologies and rule-based reasoning rather than as learned, vectorized graph tokens fed to a transformer. It models and reasons over the road environment but does not address GPS map matching or path prediction as a learning task, has no sequence model, and performs no label-free (or any) training.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination: real_gap: orthogonal symbolic-vs-learned paradigm and a BMW in-house precedent for semantic road-environment representation, not a foreshadowing of the proposed learned transformer+RL hybrid.

relevance.bmw_relevance: HIGH - this is BMW's in-house semantic-map (knowledge architecture layer) approach, authored by the thesis interview lead Adel Ayara with Birte Glimm, defining BMW's symbolic road-environment representation.
